03 / AI platforms

AgentOS — AI agents and developers building software together

It turns client requirements into tasks, runs specialised AI agents in parallel and keeps every change under review, tests and human approval.

01 / Overview

AgentOS is an autonomous development platform that coordinates software delivery between human developer teams and specialised AI agents — from the client's requirements to a tested release.

02 / The problem

Software teams lose much of their time to repetitive work: turning requirements into tickets, boilerplate code, reviews, tests and status reports. Progress, blockers and technical risks are hard to see, and handing work to AI tools without structure makes quality harder to control.

03 / Our approach

AgentOS analyses client requirements and turns them into technical tasks, splits large projects into stages and small development tasks, and assigns them to AI developer agents. Backend, frontend, QA and other specialised agents work in parallel, while automatic checks, code review, tests and human approval gates keep quality under control.

04 / The result

The aim is faster, more transparent and measurable software delivery: higher team productivity, less repetitive technical work and clear reporting on progress, blockers, risks and results. Within the ecosystem, AgentOS carries out the software tasks that RootOS and CompanyOS plan. The capabilities on this page describe the product's planned scope as development continues.

06 / Architecture

How it is built.

  1. Human in the loop

    Approval gates and quality checks keep people in control: agents propose, people approve what ships.

  2. Works where developers work

    Integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Jira and other development tools instead of replacing them.

  3. The ecosystem's developer workforce

    AgentOS executes the software tasks that come out of MeetOS decisions, RootOS priorities and CompanyOS plans.
